options: Oracle's mature, on-premises (or customer-hosted) ERP suite, first released in the late 1990s
A reporting add-on for Fusion Cloud
A new product Oracle launched in 2026
A free trial version of Oracle Fusion Cloud
questions.explain: EBS is Oracle's mature on-premises ERP suite, first released in the late 1990s, and still widely used by enterprises today.

questions.q: What does it mean that Oracle has 'repeatedly extended Premier Support' for EBS?
options: Oracle is actively building major new features into EBS every quarter
Oracle continues providing support and patches for EBS further into the future, though new strategic investment goes to Fusion Cloud
EBS has been discontinued and no longer receives any updates
EBS customers must now pay for Fusion Cloud instead
questions.explain: Extended Premier Support means ongoing patches and compliance updates continue, but Oracle's new capability investment, including AI, goes to Fusion Cloud rather than EBS.

questions.q: Which of these is a genuine difference between EBS and Fusion Cloud ERP?
options: EBS runs only in a browser, Fusion Cloud requires installed software
EBS has no Financials module; Fusion Cloud does
EBS supports deep code-level customization; Fusion Cloud is configuration-first with limited, sanctioned extension tools
Fusion Cloud is on-premises; EBS is SaaS
questions.explain: EBS, being on-premises, supports deep code customization, while multi-tenant Fusion Cloud is configuration-first by design.

questions.q: What is 'coexistence', as described in this lesson?
options: A certification exam combining EBS and Fusion Cloud topics
Two different companies using the same Oracle license
A feature that lets EBS and Fusion Cloud share the same login screen
Running EBS and Fusion Cloud together, often during a gradual migration
questions.explain: Coexistence describes an organization running EBS and Fusion Cloud side by side, often for different business units during a gradual migration.

questions.q: Why does this course and career path focus on Fusion Cloud rather than EBS?
options: New Oracle ERP implementations are overwhelmingly choosing Fusion Cloud, and that's where Oracle's roadmap and new investment are headed
EBS has been completely shut down by Oracle
EBS and Fusion Cloud are identical, so it doesn't matter which is taught
Fusion Cloud requires no accounting knowledge at all
questions.explain: New implementations favor Fusion Cloud, Oracle's own product investment goes there, and its configuration-first skill set transfers more easily between employers.
